facts.fact: The National Department of Health's bid terms of reference state that under the District Health Management Information System Policy the Director-General has overall ownership of the system, that all its data is owned by the Department of Health, and that every change to the system must be authorised by the department; the bidder may not share the data.

The National Department of Health itself invites bids, under National Treasury prescripts and priced in rand, for three years of hosting, maintenance, support and enhancement of the system; the bid names no funder other than the department and gives no contract value or budget line.

The department describes the system as an aggregated service delivery information system used at facility, district, province and national level, reporting by facility type (clinic, community health centre, hospitals), and plans user training at primary health care clinics, community health centres, district, regional and tertiary or central hospitals.

The department states that nine provincial instances capture the routine data while the national instance captures nothing directly and is filled by synchronisation; that the system offers offline entry by web or mobile; that all health facilities must reconcile source documents monthly against the databases they are captured into; and that 920 data capturers at primary health care clinics and 400 at district hospitals are to be trained over three years.

On 24 July 2026 the National Department of Health issued bid NDOH 09/2025-2026 (closing 25 August 2026) for a service provider to host, maintain, support and enhance the existing system for three years, covering nine provincial DHIS2 instances and the national data warehouse and competency-based training of about 6,000 officials (2,059 in year 1, 2,059 in year 2, 1,882 in year 3).
